DILG Republic of the Philippines DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT DILG-NAPOLCOM Center, EDSA corner Quezon Avenue, West Triangle, Quezon City http: //WMN.dilg.com.ph FEB 04 2020 OPINION NO. MR. JESUS F. FUME-RA Chairman of the Board Sorsogon City Water District Capito! Compound, Sorsogon City 4700 Dear Mr. Fumera: This has reference to the indorsement dated 20 September 2019 from Atty. Elpidio J. Vega, Government Corporate Counsel, Office of the Government Corporate Counsel, requesting for this Department's advice on the resignation of the Board of Directors of Sorsogon City Water District upon the request of the Sanggunian of Sorsogon City. In the attached Board Resolution No. 012-19 (Reso 012-19) of the Board of Directors of Sorsogon City Water District (SCWD), it is stated that the City Council of Sorsogon City passed Resolution No. 004, series of 2019 requesting the City Mayor to replace the existing composition of the Board of Directors of the SCWD / Prime Water. It is also stated that the same City Council passed another resolution, Resolution No. 035, series of 2019, requesting the current Board of Directors to tender courtesy resignation for the purpose of the appointment and reappointment of new set of Board of Directors thereof. Accordingly, the Board of Directors of SCWD tenders its resignation in the same Board Resolution (Reso 012-19). We are of the view that the interference of the Sanggunian through said Resolutions is not in harmony with the provisions of Presidential Decree No. 198 (PD 198), series of 1973, which includes Local Water District Law. We fine Section 6 thereof relevant. It clearly states: "Section 6. Formation of District. - This Act is the source of authorization and power to form and maintain a district. Once formed, a district is subject to the provisions of this Act and not under the jurisdiction of any political subdivision. To form a district, the legislative body of any city, municipality or province shall enact a resolution containing the following: (a) The name of the local water district, which shall include the name of the city, municipality, or province, or region

thereof, served by said system, followed by the words "Water District". (b) A description of the boundary of the district. In the case of a city or municipality, such boundary may include all lands within the city or municipality. A district may include one or more municipalities, cities or provinces, or portions thereof. (c) A statement of intent to transfer any and a!l waterworks and/or sewerage facilities owned by such city, municipality or province to such district pursuant to a contract authorized by Section 31 (b) of this Title. (d) A statement identifying the purpose for which the district is formed, which shall include those purposes outlined in Section 5 above. (e) The names of the initial directors of the district with the date of expiration of term of office for each. (f) A statement that the district may only be dissolved on the grounds and under the conditions set forth in Section 44 of this Title. (g) A statement acknowledging the powers, rights and obligations as set forth in Section 36 of this Title. Nothing in the resolution of formation shall state or infer that the local legislative body has the power to dissolve, alter or affect the district beyond that specifically provided for in this Act. If two or more cities, municipalities or provinces, or any combination thereof, desire to form a single district, a similar resolution shall be adopted in each city, municipality and province. " In PD 198, as amended, at most, the participation of the Local Government Unit is in the formation of the water district. There is nothing in the law where the interference of local officials can stand on. In fact, this Department has been consistent that the LGUs shall strictly observe the operational autonomy of the local water districts (DILG Memorandum Circular No. 2016-146, dated 18 October 2016 and DILG Memorandum Circular No. 2019-03, dated IO January 2019). This Department has reiterated that the laws, rules and regulations as follows shall be strictly complied with by ail LGUs: I. Water Districts once formed, are subject to provisions of Presidential Decree (PD) No. 198, as amended and not under the jurisdiction of any political subdivision (Section 6 of PD 198, DILG Memorandum Circular No. 88-15 dated 01 March 1988, DILG Memorandum Circular

No. 97-98 dated April 15, 19978 and DILG Memorandum Circular Nc. 2005-21 dated March 4, 2005); 2. 3. Water Districts are autonomous agencies independent of local governments. It should be best that they are allowed to operate the least hindrance and interference from the local officials but with a maximum support and assistance (Section 6, PD 198, DILG Memorandum Circular NO. 88-15 dated 01 March 1988, DILG Memorandum Circular No. 97-98 dated April 14, 29987 and DILG Memorandum Circular No. 2005-21 dated March 4, 2005); and While the Local Government Code provides for the legal basis relative to the devolution powers, functions and attributes granted by law to the Local Water Utilities Administration to local water districts, should they opt to exercise such powers, functions and attributes, there is nothing in the Code that indicates that it has repeated the pertinent provisions Presidential Decree No. 198, as amended (Sections 530 and 534 of Local Government Code (RA 7160) and DILG Memorandum Circular No. 97-98 dated April 14, 19987 and DILG Memorandum Circular No. 2005-21 dated March 4, 2005).2 Further, Section 5 of Presidential Decree No. 768, series of 1975, the law amending PD 198, it provides that the Directors of local water districts have a term of office and that they may only be removed for cause and subject to the review and approval of the Local Water Utilities Administration. Section 5 thereof states: Section 5. Section II of the same decree is hereby amended to read as follows: "Sec. 11. Term of Office. Of the five initial directors of each newly-formed district, two shall be appointed for a maximum term of two years, two for a maximum term of four years, and one for a maximum term of six years. Terms of office of all directors in a given district shall be such that the term of at least one director, but not more than two, shall expire on December 31 of each even-numbered year. Regular terms of office after the initial terms shall be for six years commencing on January 1 of odd-numbered years. Directors may be removed for cause only, subject to review and approval of the Administration. " DILG Memorandum Circular NO. 2019-03

In view of the foregoing, we further reiterate that the LGUs shall refrain from any interference that may violate the operational autonomy of the local water districts. We hope that we have enlightened you on the matter. Thank you. Very Y yours, ED D Copy furnished: ATTY. ELPIDIO J. VEGA Government Corporate Counsel, Office of the Government Corporate Counsel Department of Justice ANO
